A controlled fork (same code, same rules, one thing changed) is exactly the infrastructure that re-send step needs and doesn't exist anywhere else in the strategy doc's M5 description by name -- but the doc never assigns worktree mechanics to M5 explicitly either (its two literal 'worktree' mentions sit at M1 pre-reads and an M6 scheduled-agents callout, not M5). This file's own maintainer block supplies the missing provenance: extracted verbatim, 2026-08-12, Antti-directed, from module prose that already lived at this exact point in M5 ('this and next slide should be part of exercise module'). No downstream M5 teaching moment (three-pattern, verifier-build, reference+plan assembly) is spoiled or pre-taught by this file -- it only sets up the environment those beats run in. Front-run absent; Big Idea (split-test discipline) matches the file's own point line; module-to-module handoff is intact per the maintainer block's explicit placement note (immediately before diagnose-and-resend.md, which opens inside the worktree this file creates).
